text: This chunk discusses the diagnosis of cholera, emphasizing that doctors diagnose based on symptoms, disease exposure history, stool characteristics, and stool examination. It mentions that stool culture is the most definitive test but can take 2-3 days, often only confirming the diagnosis after symptoms have resolved. For patients with severe, uncontrollable watery diarrhea in endemic areas, doctors suspect cholera and immediately start treatment with oral rehydration salts (ORS) or intravenous fluids. Physical examination typically shows no fever, minimal abdominal pain, and varying degrees of dehydration, with severe cases presenting shock and rapid breathing due to acidosis. In children, fever, seizures, lethargy, or unconsciousness may be observed.
